The delete flow (useDeleteModal / DeleteModal) needs to support deletion by identifier (ruleSourceName + uid) without a RulerRuleDTO, as RuleActionsButtons.V2 already does via getEditableIdentifier.

findings.title: DeclareIncidentMenuItem receives an empty url and promRule.name without null check
findings.body: shouldShowDeclareIncidentButton checks `prometheusRuleType.alertingRule(promRule) && promRule.state === PromAlertingRuleState.Firing`, but prometheusRuleType.alertingRule only checks rule.type === 'alerting' — it does not guarantee promRule is defined (the type guard accepts `rule?: Rule`). If promRule is undefined, `promRule.state` throws a TypeError. In the list view promRule is always provided for grafana rules, but AlertRuleMenu is also used from the rule viewer where promRule may be absent while rulerRule is present; in that case shouldShowDeclareIncidentButton would crash. The guard must check promRule is defined before accessing promRule.state, and DeclareIncidentMenuItem is passed url={''} which produces a broken incident link.

findings.title: Silence drawer is gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), so silencing never opens in the list view where rule (ruler rule) is undefined
findings.body: The silence drawer renders only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, and SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer receives `rulerRule={rule}`. In the list view, RuleActionsButtons is rendered with only promRule (no ruler rule — see GrafanaRuleListItem which passes only promRule), so `rule` is undefined, the condition is false, and clicking 'Silence notifications' in the AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer=true but no drawer ever opens. The silence flow must be adapted to work with GrafanaPromRuleDTO (which has uid, folderUid, name) instead of requiring a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO.

findings.title: handleDelete uses identifier-based delete modal but AlertRuleMenu's internal delete path still expects a ruler rule
findings.body: RuleActionsButtons passes `handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}` to AlertRuleMenu, but AlertRuleMenu's Props declare `handleDelete: (rule: RulerRuleDTO, groupIdentifier: RuleGroupIdentifierV2) => void` and its Delete menu item calls `handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)`. This is a type mismatch: the menu will call the handler with (rulerRule, groupIdentifier) while the handler ignores its arguments and uses the closure `identifier`. It happens to work because the handler ignores arguments, but the Props contract is wrong and the Delete menu item is additionally gated on `rulerRule` being truthy (see separate finding), so in the list view the menu's Delete item never renders and this handler is effectively dead code from the menu. The AlertRuleMenu Props should be changed to `handleDelete: () => void` (or the menu should use the identifier), and the gating fixed.

findings.title: Removing the ruler fetch eliminates 'Creating'/'Deleting' rule states from the group list
findings.body: The previous implementation matched ruler rules against prom rules and rendered rules that exist only in the ruler with RuleOperation.Creating, and rules that exist only in Prometheus (already removed from ruler but not yet propagated) with RuleOperation.Deleting via RuleOperationListItem. The new implementation renders only promResponse rules, so: (1) a newly created rule will not appear in the list until Prometheus evaluates it (previously it appeared immediately with a 'Creating' indicator), and (2) a deleted rule disappears from the list immediately instead of showing a 'Deleting' state until propagation completes. This is a deliberate product change perhaps, but it also means the 'Creating'/'Deleting' UI states and the matchRules consistency warning (which logged when a ruler rule had no Prometheus counterpart) are gone entirely. If the intent was only to remove per-rule ruler requests, the group-level ruler fetch (one request per group, already cached/prefetched) could have preserved these states. At minimum this behavioral regression should be called out and confirmed as intended; the removed tests in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists') confirm the states are no longer supported.

findings.title: Error handling only covers missing promResponse, not query errors
findings.body: The component checks `if (!promResponse)` to show an error Alert, but useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery's error state is not checked. If the Prometheus groups request fails (network error, 500), promResponse will be undefined and the generic 'Failed to load rules' alert shows — acceptable — but with RTK Query, a failed request followed by a successful retry or a cached undefined could mask errors; more importantly, the previous implementation distinguished ruler vs prom errors (RulerRuleLoadingError). Now a transient prom error permanently shows the error Alert with no retry mechanism other than the polling interval refetch. Consider checking `error` from the query and only showing the Alert when there's no data after loading completes.

findings.title: Redundant double type check for alerting rules
findings.body: The component first checks `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (which already verifies rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting plus folderUid/uid presence), then inside computes `const promAlertingRule = rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined;` — repeating the same type check. The inner check is redundant; `rule` can be used directly. Not a bug per se, but it suggests confusion about the type narrowing and could mask a mismatch if the two checks ever diverge.

findings.title: View link omits returnTo parameter that the old GrafanaRuleListItem included
findings.body: The old GrafanaRuleListItem (in deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule view returned to the list with filters intact. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without returnTo. This breaks the 'return to list' UX: after viewing a rule, the back navigation loses the list filter/scroll state. The returnTo should be restored.

findings.title: skipToken sentinel exported and threaded through public ability hooks is a fragile API contract
findings.body: A module-level Symbol `skipToken` is exported and accepted by useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities to mean 'skip this rule'. Callers must remember to pass skipToken when the rule is not a Grafana prom rule (e.g. `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken`). If a caller passes undefined instead, useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) runs the full hook (folder fetch, config status query) and returns abilities computed for a non-existent rule — mostly [false, false] but with wasted queries and potentially wrong 'supported' flags (e.g. Silence supported=true with allowed=false). The skipToken pattern is error-prone; a cleaner contract would be to accept `GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined` and return all-unsupported abilities for undefined, or split into a separate hook used only when the rule is known to be Grafana-managed. At minimum, passing a non-Grafana prom rule (not skipToken) would compute abilities against getRulesPermissions('grafana') incorrectly.

findings.title: Grafana prom rule Silence ability drops the 'not a recording rule' check present in the ruler-based hook
findings.body: In useAllRulerRuleAbilities, Silence ability comes from useCanSilence(rule), which returns [false, false] when the rule is a Grafana recording rule (`isGrafanaRecording` check). In the new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, Silence is `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` where isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) — this checks type === 'alerting', so recording rules are excluded from the allowed side but `silenceSupported` (the first tuple element) is true for recording rules. Since Ability = [supported, allowed] and consumers check `supported && allowed`, recording rules still won't show silence. However the 'supported' flag being true for recording rules is semantically wrong and any consumer that only checks `supported` (or uses the tuple loosely) would incorrectly enable silence for recording rules. The ruler-based useCanSilence also verified the rule is a Grafana-managed alerting rule; the prom-based version should mirror that by gating both elements on isAlertingRule.

findings.title: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities marks rules as supported while folder permissions are still loading, and never reflects ruler availability
findings.body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported` — unlike the ruler-based hook which uses isRulerAvailable. For Grafana-managed rules this is mostly fine (Grafana always has a ruler), but combined with useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable: when the folder is still loading, `loading` is true so MaybeSupported=false — good. However when `!rule || !folderUID`, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns `{isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false}` — so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported=true even though there is no rule. Abilities for a non-existent rule then report supported=true (e.g. Duplicate: [true, rulesPermissions.create]). Any caller that checks only the supported flag (or ORs abilities across rule types as AlertRuleMenu does) could surface actions for a rule that doesn't exist. The hook should return all-NotSupported abilities when rule is undefined, similar to how useCanSilence returns [false,false] for missing rules.

findings.title: Test asserts exactly 4 menu items but Delete is missing from the menu in the list view (test passes only because Delete is broken)
findings.body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' asserts `menuItems.length` is 4 (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) and never asserts that Delete is present, even though the test's beforeEach grants AlertingRuleDelete permission and folder delete permission. Given that AlertRuleMenu gates the Delete item on `rulerRule` being defined (which is undefined in this list view), Delete is silently absent. The test therefore enshrines the broken behavior: a user with delete permission cannot delete a rule from the list. The test should assert the Delete menu item is present (and add a negative-permission case), which would currently fail and expose the bug.

findings.title: Permission-denied test only checks the Edit button, not the More menu actions
findings.body: The test 'should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions' overrides folder access control to deny update/delete but only asserts the Edit link is absent and the More button is present. It does not verify that the Delete menu item is hidden in the More menu when delete permission is denied (the beforeEach granted delete permission, and this test denies it via setFolderAccessControl). Since the menu's delete/pause/silence visibility depends on the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities hook, a regression that shows Delete (or Pause) to unauthorized users would not be caught.

findings.title: Test names say 'Should not render' but the mock grants the permission (isEditable: true)
findings.body: The tests are titled 'Should not render Edit button for users with the update permission' and mock useIsRuleEditable to return { isEditable: true }, then assert the Edit button is NOT in the document. Either the test titles are wrong (they should say 'without the update permission' and mock isEditable: false), or the assertions are inverted. As written, the tests assert that a user WITH edit permission does not see the Edit button — which contradicts the intended RBAC behavior and would only pass if the Edit button is broken for authorized users. The mock values and titles are inconsistent; one of them must be fixed, otherwise the test validates the wrong behavior.

findings.title: beforeEach calls jest.resetAllMocks() after setting up mocks, and mock setup order is fragile
findings.body: The beforeEach calls jest.clearAllMocks(), jest.restoreAllMocks(), jest.resetAllMocks() and then sets default mock return values. jest.resetAllMocks() resets mock implementations, so setting defaults afterwards is correct, but jest.restoreAllMocks() only affects spies created with jest.spyOn — combined with the module-level jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities'), the triple-reset pattern is redundant and confusing. More importantly, several tests then override only some of the five mocked hooks (e.g. the Grafana 'Should not render Delete button' test sets useAlertRuleAbility and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities but relies on the beforeEach default [false,false] for useRulerRuleAbilities). Because AlertRuleMenu ORs ruler and grafana abilities, a test that intends 'no delete permission' could accidentally pass or fail depending on which hook path the component takes. The tests would be more robust if each test explicitly mocked all hooks it depends on, or if the component under test used a single ability source.

findings.title: Stale comment about preloading ruler rules
findings.body: The comment above the populateCache block still says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded' — but the ruler prefetch (alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)) was removed in this PR. The comment now describes behavior that no longer exists and should be updated to reflect that only the Prometheus groups cache is populated.

findings.title: useAllAlertRuleAbilities marked @deprecated but still used by useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities which are not deprecated
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities is annotated '@deprecated Use {@link useAllRulerRuleAbilities} instead', but the non-deprecated public hooks useAlertRuleAbility and useAlertRuleAbilities (used by RuleActionsButtons and others) still call it internally. The deprecation is misleading: consumers of useAlertRuleAbility cannot migrate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities without also reimplementing the groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule mapping. Either deprecate the whole CombinedRule-based API surface consistently or remove the misleading annotation.

findings.title: RuleActionsButtons receives promRule typed as Rule but GrafanaRuleListItem passes GrafanaPromRuleDTO; pause/delete/silence actions in the menu are broken for list-view Grafana rules
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem renders <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact /> where rule is GrafanaPromRuleDTO. RuleActionsButtons passes promRule to AlertRuleMenu, which uses it for grafana abilities (correct), but the menu's Pause item requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) (undefined in list view → hidden), Delete requires rulerRule (undefined → hidden), and the silence drawer in RuleActionsButtons requires rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where rule is the ruler rule prop (undefined → drawer never opens). Net effect: in the new list view, Grafana-managed rules lose Pause, Delete, and Silence actions from the UI even for fully authorized users. This is the core functional regression of removing the ruler from the list view; the actions must be reimplemented against GrafanaPromRuleDTO/identifier-based APIs.
